rules.text: TS Series worksurfaces have a wood core with a High-Pressure or Low-Pressure Laminate surface and are 1 3/16" thick; laminate top with plastic edge band. Full-depth worksurfaces fit flush against panels.

Both Low-Pressure Laminate (LPL) and High-Pressure Laminate (HPL) are available (except linking worksurfaces: HPL only). Plastic edge band color is selectable and specified separately from laminate color.

Front (user's) edge is a plastic edge band with a 3 mm radius; back and side edges are flat. Edge profile is applied to front (user's) edge only. Back and side edge plastic color defaults to match user's edge.

PVC-free 3 mm edge profiles are a proprietary polyolefin blend for all solid colors and seven woodgrain finishes; matching 1 mm side and back edges are also PVC-free. See surface material listing for PVC-free availability.

Grommet is standard on corner worksurfaces only (straight corner, curved corner, LH/RH extended curved corner, 120° corner). Field-installed grommet (TSAEGROM package) requires a 3" diameter hole in the worksurface.
Corner bracket is included with corner worksurfaces to connect the back corner of the worksurface to panels.

30"D straight and transition cantilevered worksurfaces require additional floor support along the front edge, such as a pedestal, end panel, post leg, side support bracket, or an adjacent return worksurface. (p181 also lists 30"D tapered.)
Spanner worksurfaces with 3" notch accommodate Kick panels. Legs and cantilevers or column and cantilevers must be used for support.
Specify two cantilevers (TSATCANT) and a post leg (TSATP27) to attach a spanner worksurface to adjacent worksurfaces (tip refers to 50" and 62" spanner tops; listed widths are 51" and 63").
Linking worksurfaces with 3" notch accommodate Answer panels. One leg and two cantilevers must be used to support linking worksurfaces.
Order cantilevers (TSATCANT, p503) to connect linking worksurfaces to adjacent worksurfaces.

Bullet peninsula, angled peninsula, and jetty worksurfaces can be supported two ways: (1) with a cantilever, a center support panel, and a column; or (2) with a cantilever, a side support bracket, and two post legs.

Supports are ordered separately and installed in the field. Supports available for use with Kick (TS Series) worksurfaces: post leg, H-leg, cantilever with tie plate, side support brackets, tie plates, in-line support plate, reinforcing channel, on-module end panel.

Long worksurface spans must be supported with cantilevers, pedestals, legs, or other supports at least every 54". Reinforcing channel allows the distance between supports to be increased to 60" for worksurfaces that will be heavily loaded, or up to 72" for worksurfaces with lighter expected loads. Reinforcing channel must be specified separately.

Page 177/181 name the reinforcing channel as TS7WKSPT (Universal Systems, spec p546); the TS Series page 503 lists TSATRC39/48/57/72. p183 cites TSATRC57 for heavily loaded worksurfaces with 60" or more unsupported kneespace.
LPL and HPL worksurfaces differ slightly in actual thickness and may differ in sheen/texture; specify only one worksurface type (LPL or HPL) within a given application.

Open Line laminate program (non-Steelcase laminates suitable for Steelcase products) is available on High-Pressure Laminate worksurfaces only: +$65 plus cost of laminate; see Surface Materials Reference Manual.

Kick (TS Series) is available in a wide variety of worksurface shapes; directional laminate grain direction for each shape (straight, transition, straight corner, curved corner, LH/RH extended curved corner, 120° corner, peninsula, angled peninsula, spanner) is shown by arrows in the p177 illustrations (grain generally runs along the longest dimension).

Identical worksurfaces ordered on the same line item are packed on pallets containing 10-20 worksurfaces; remaining worksurfaces are packed individually in cartons. If palletizing is not desired, order in quantities of nine or less per line item.

HPLs are more durable (7-15 layers of resin-soaked paper) and cost more; generally used in higher-traffic areas (cafeterias, conference rooms). LPLs (melamine-dipped paper bonded to wood core) suit lower-impact areas, vertical applications, and workstation/private office tops.

On-module worksurface supports engage the slots in the vertical uprights of Kick panels. On-module supports can be used to panel-support worksurfaces in various configurations (see Specifying page 545 for panel-mounted Universal Systems supports for Answer panels).
End panel can be used to support the end of a worksurface at standard seated height (TSATEP24/30, 27"H) or standing height (TSATEP24S/30S, 40"H).

End panels can be used to support the end of a worksurface for additional panel stability (refer to panel stability guidelines). End panels are available in seated and standing heights and cannot be used in freestanding applications.
Side support brackets support worksurfaces at any height in 1" increments. Brackets ship as a left- and right-hand pair (TSATSIDE) and are ordered separately.

Side support brackets can support the ends of straight and corner worksurfaces and the back corner of any corner worksurface; they can support the end of a worksurface that is wrapped by a panel with the same width dimension that matches the worksurface depth.
A single side support bracket can be used to support the rear corner of corner, extended corner, and 120° corner worksurfaces. It is standard with these corner worksurfaces.
Cantilever can be used to panel-support a worksurface at any height.

Cantilevers support worksurfaces at any height in 1" increments. Cantilever is non-handed and can be used to support either end of a worksurface, or shared to support two worksurfaces at the same height simultaneously. One tie plate ships with each cantilever.
All panel-mounted supports can be removed and repositioned later without any permanent damage to panels or skins.
Pedestals and lateral files with a filler can be used to support the end of a worksurface in place of an end panel.
Worksurfaces used in panel-supported installations must follow applicable panel stability guidelines (page 124).

Side support bracket and reinforcing channel: black paint only. Cantilever, center support panel, and end panel: paint (color selectable). Post legs and H-legs: paint price groups 1-3 (No cost/+$12/+$23). On-module end panel: paint price groups 1-3 (No cost/+$28/+$47). Tie plates and in-line support plates: black paint.
Post leg has 2" adjustable glides; H-legs have 2 3/4" adjustable glides; center support panel and end panel glide range 1 1/4"; cantilever N.A.

Freestanding guidelines: consult local dealer or Steelcase representative prior to deviating from these guidelines. Ends of a freestanding worksurface can be supported with post legs, a 20"W H-leg, or a 22"D or 28"D pedestal.
Single freestanding worksurface supported by 20"W H-leg: 72" max. width. Supported by a 22"D or 28"D pedestal at one end: 72" max. width.
20"W H-leg can support adjacent worksurfaces up to 72"W each (72" max. + 72" max., post legs at outer ends).
Combined worksurfaces can give each other support when joined with an 11"W H-leg and tie plate.

Corner worksurface attached to adjacent worksurfaces requires an 11"W H-leg (TSATH2711). Tie plate is recommended to align worksurfaces. This application is only good for 48"W corner worksurfaces; the 36"W and 42"W corner worksurfaces do not meet ADA requirements.
11"W H-leg can be used to support a corner worksurface and adjacent worksurfaces up to 72"W (diagram: 72" max. + 72" max. along one side, 48" max. return).
120° worksurface freestanding: 11"W H-leg, tie plates and post legs; diagram limits 36" max. on one side and 114" max. on the other.
H-leg can be used to support adjacent perpendicular worksurfaces up to 72"W (diagram: 72" max. by 72" max. with peninsula end).
11"W H-leg can be used to support a corner worksurface and adjacent worksurfaces up to 72"W; U-configuration with peninsula: peninsula 60" or 72" only, corner return 48" only, other run 72" max.
Reinforcing channel (TSATRC57) is available to add support to worksurfaces that have 60" or more of unsupported kneespace and that are heavily loaded.

Cross-reference (outside this section): panel-mounted supports for Answer panels are on Universal Systems spec pages 545-547 - on-module cantilever UCANT, side support brackets USSBR (only one of the handed pair is required for rear-corner support of a panel-mounted corner worksurface; specify one per two corner worksurfaces on-module), support plates TS714WSP/TS720WSP, tie plates TS7TIEPLATE, reinforcing channels TS7WKSPT39/TS7WKSPT/TS7WKSPT72, center support panels (p547). Answer panel junctions can accommodate only one cantilever at a seam. No panel-width-based cantilever/end-support table exists in the TS Series pages 171-184/489-504.

Worksurface-height power and communication access (page 555) is listed as a related product for straight, transition, straight corner, curved corner, extended curved corner, 120° corner and linking worksurfaces (not for peninsula, angled peninsula, spanner).

unresolved: p496 vs p174: 120° corner overall dimension D printed as 63 11/32" and 85 5/32" on spec p496 but 62 11/32" and 83 5/32" on Statement of Line p174 (72 3/4" agrees). Geometry (B x sqrt3) supports p174; p496 values likely misprints. Both recorded.
p499 spanner tip says '50" and 62" spanner tops' while the table lists 51" and 63" widths (TSAWLN51A/TSAWLN63A); presumably the same products.

p494/p495: RH extended corner style numbers are not simple mirrors of LH digit order in terms of which run carries the 24" vs 30" depth (e.g., LH E2364 and RH E2346 share identical prices). A/B semantics recorded per spec-page diagrams (A = end depth of C run, B = end depth of D run); verify with Steelcase before relying on A/B for geometry.
p180: H-leg actual depths 14" or 22 3/4" are not explicitly tied to 11"W vs 20"W; mapping (11W->14, 20W->22 3/4) is inferred and recorded only in notes.

p177/p181 cite reinforcing channel 'TS7WKSPT' (Universal Systems, p546) whereas TS spec p503 lists TSATRC39/48/57/72; p183 cites TSATRC57. Both families exist; which is preferred for Kick worksurfaces is not stated.
Transition worksurfaces: 'deeperEnd' (left/right) derived from diagram orientation (A left, B right) on p172/p491; the guide does not use the word 'handed' for transitions.
Linking worksurfaces: Statement of Line p175 area drawings do not label left/right, so areas (678/840/840/996) were not mapped to individual styles.

Cantilever (TSATCANT) paint color is specifiable per p502 exception, but no paint price-group upcharge is listed for it; center support panel referenced on p177/p180/p181 is not in the TS spec pages (see Universal Systems p547).
The guide provides no table of required cantilevers/end supports by panel width for TS Series worksurfaces; support requirements are captured as rules only.
